stem: Which one of the following is not an genetic disease?
expl: Night blindness is not a genetic disease. The cause of Night blindness is deficiency of vitamin A. Albinism is genetic disease in which the pigments called melanin is partially or completely absent in the skin, hair and eyes. Haemophilia is a genetic sex-linked disease. Colour blindness is also a genetic disease.

stem: Phenylketonuria is an example of an inborn error of metabolism. This ‘error’ refers to :
expl: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a disease caused by a metabolic disorder inherited as a recessive trait. It is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of amino acid phenylalanine. The dominant gene ‘P’, in this case, codes for the enzyme, phenylalanine hydroxylase, formed in the liver cells. This enzyme catalyzes conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine. In homozygous recessive genotypes, the absence of this enzyme causes a high level of phenylalanine in blood and tissues fluids. The phenotypic effects include a progressive mental retardation starting a few month after birth, seizures, and anomalies of teeth enamel and bones.

stem: Haemophilia is a genetic disease carried by –
expl: Haemophilia is a genetic sex-linked disease in which blood clotting takes a long time in a patient (up to 24 hours) due to lack of thromboplastin protein in blood plasma. Women carry it while it appears in men (because men have one X-chromosome but women have two). It is also called bleeder’s disease which was first found in Queen Victoria. So it is also known as ‘royal haemophilia’ or ‘the royal disease’.

stem: Which of the following is not a genetic disorder?
expl: Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle cell anaemia are hereditary diseases. Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is not a genetic disorder, it is a common gut disorder. The cause is not well known. Symptoms can be quite variable and include tummy (abdominal) pain, bloating and sometimes bouts of diarrhoea and/or constipation.

stem: In humans trisomy of chromosome number 21 is responsible for :
expl: Down Syndrome, also known as trisomy 21, is a genetic disorder caused by the presence of all or part of the third copy of chromosome 21. It is usually associated with physical growth delays, mild to moderate intellectual disability, and characteristic facial features. It is also known as Mongolian idiocy.

stem: In respect of women, men can suffer more of colour blindness because–

options.label: a
options.text: They pass more through mental tensions

options.label: b
options.text: They live out of home relatively more

expl: Colour blindness is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The genes are located on the X-chromosome which is one of the two sex chromosomes. In males (who have only one X-chromosome) one genetic change in each cell is sufficient to cause the condition. Males are affected by X-linked recessive disorders much more frequently than females (who have two X-chromosomes) in which a genetic change would have to occur on both copies of the chromosome to cause the disorder. A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that father cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons.

stem: If a colour blind man marries with normal women, then the symptoms of colour blindness is generated in :
expl: If a colour blind man marries with a normal woman, they produce normal sons and heterozygous (carrier) normal daughter. If a carrier daughter is then married to a normal husband, about 50% of their sons and daughters will inherit the recessive gene of colour blindness. The sons inheriting this gene will be colour blind and the daughters will be carriers. The remaining 50% sons and daughters will be normal.
